questionStem: An otherwise healthy 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of a pigmented lesion under the nail of her ring finger. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
correctExplanation: Appropriate in view of the medical necessity to remove the inflamed appendix • Acutely inflamed appendix is a medical emergency and therefore doesn't require consent.
Aldosteronoma • Hyperaldosteronism → hypokalemia • Aldosterone escape → normal Na levels
Ruptured spleen • Kehr sign: referred pain in shoulder due to irritants (eg, blood) in the peritoneal cavity • Kehr sign in the left shoulder is a classic sxs of a ruptured spleen
High-output congesting heart failure • Circulatory overload → ↑ diastolic pressure in LV → pulmonary edema
Squamous cell carcinoma • SCC → PTHrP → hypercalcemia

Needle-localized open biopsy • Percutaneous core biopsy, localization with needle and surgically sampling, is preferred for evaluation of microcalcifications • Fine-needle aspiration is inadequate as it may miss the cancer cells
Cardiogenic shock • SOB, JVD, hypotension, hepatomegaly, ST elevation in anterior leads
Testicular tumor • Young age, painless progressive enlargement over 8 months = cancer • Hydrocele and Spermatocele both transilluminate • Epididymitis is painful
Rapid infusion of 0.9% saline • Patient is unstable
Cytomegalovirus • Colitis in HIV + nuclear inclusion bodies = CMV • Presents with hematochezia, abdominal pain, weight loss, low-grade feve
Lactated Ringer solution • Ranson's criteria → pancreatitis • Rx: fluids, analgesics, NPO
Sphenopalatine artery • Sphenopalatine artery is the MCC of posterior nosebleeds • 90% of nosebleeds are anteriorly located at Kiesselbach's plexus
15 L of lactated Ringer solution • Parkland formula: 4 x weight in kg x % body surface area that is burnt • 4 × 75 × 50 = 15000 ml = 15L
Bladder outflow obstruction • Old male with mass in lower quadrant indicated BPH
Fat embolism • Associated with long bone fractures and liposuction • Triad: Neurologic dysfunction, petechial rash (usually in axilla), respiratory distress (hypoxemia) • Therapy is supportive
Pseudomonas species • Gram negative rod
Incision and drainage of the lesion • Abscesses must be drained
Surgical decompression • Compartment syndrome • Paresthesia and pain on passive stretch are early sxs
Lack of normal joint sensation • Neuropathic (Charcot) arthropathy

Aortic arteriography • Mild tenderness over the chest and a 'somewhat' widened mediastinum warrant an aortic arteriography • If the patient had presented with "tearing chest pain radiating to the back" and a widened mediastinum following a MVC, then an immediate thoracotomy would be indicated
Water-soluble contrast upper gastrointestinal study • Rupture/perforation is a complication of esophagoscopy • Water-soluble (gastrograffin) contrast study can diagnose rupture

Initiation of dialysis • 1 urea nitrogen must be corrected pre-operatively because 1 urea → platelet dysfunction → hemorrhage during surgery • Decompression (DDAVP) → ↑ release of factor VIII/vWf multimers, which can correct the coagulopathy in uremic patients
Low-dose heparin prophylaxis (not sure) • Heparin is best choice for pre-surgical VTE prophylaxis because it has a short half-life (~45 mins) and is easily reversed with protamine sulfate

Epidural hematoma • The middle meningeal artery runs underneath the pterion, the weak region of the skull where the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones join together • Traumatic blows to this area classically cause an epidural hematoma
Femoral hernia • Protrudes through femoral canal lateral to the pubic tubercle and medial to the femoral vessels
Sliding hiatal hernia • Sliding hiatal hernias account for >90% of hiatal hernias • Associated with GERD and reflux esophagitis → ↑ risk of Barrett's esophagus
Failure to suppress class Il antigen recognition in the host • Acute rejection has an onset of weeks to months • CD4 against MHC class Il antigen
Increased serum aldosterone concentration • Renin increases on the affected side due to ↓ blood supply → ↑ aldosterone • Blood supply to unaffected side is normal, so no need to release renin

Glucagonoma (not sure) • Glucagonomas: diarrhea, dermatitis, declining weight which are some of the (D)s of glucagonoma. • Insulinoma presents with recurrent fasting hypoglycemia • VIPoma is associated with MEN 1 syndrome and presents with WDHA syndrome (Watery Diarrhea, Hypokalemia, Achlorhydria)
Increase positive end-expiratory pressure • Normal PO2 is between 80-10 • FiO2 and PEEP determine PO2; • Tidal volume and RR determine PCO2

Proctocolectomy with an ileoanal reservoir • Prophylactic colectomy is the best long-term management in FAP because 100% of cases will eventually progress to CRC • FAP patients should be screened with a colonoscopy every year starting at age 10-12
Clostridium perfringens • Crepitus - gas-forming = clostridium

Laparotomy • Presence of peritoneal signs in a patient with acute abdomen = indication for ex-lap • Presence of involuntary guarding and rigidity is a contraindication for colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy
Thoracic spinal cord • Breast cancer metastasis to spinal cord • Decreased sensation below T4 indicates a thoracic location
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia • Antibody-heparin-PF4 complex activates platelets → thrombosis and thrombocytopenia
RBC 30/hpf (in sediment) • Hematuria, gross or microscopic, occurs in the majority of patients with symptomatic nephrolithiasis
Atrial myxoma • Obstruction of mitral valve in diastole → diastolic murmur • Changing of positions → movement of tumor → disappearance of murmur • Cardiac myxoma produce IL-6 → fever and weight loss

Gastric bypass • This patients has comorbidities due to morbid obesity (she is most likely bed-ridden → poor personal hygiene) • BMI > 35 with a major comorbidity (eg, HTN, DM, etc.) qualifies for bariatric surgery; BMI > 40 qualifies without the presence of comorbidities

Ovarian adenocarcinoma • Nulligravid → uninterrupted menstrual cycles (follicular rupture and tissue damage) → ↑ risk of ovarian cancer • Advanced ovarian cancer → peritoneal seeding and inflammation → ascites • Meigs syndrome: triad of ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion
Lymphoma • Lymphatic obstruction (eg, neoplasm) → chylous ascites

Formation of antiplatelet antibodies • Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) causes destruction of platelets in the spleen due to anti- Gpllb/Illa antibodies • Labs: ↑ megakaryocytes, ↓ platelets • Treatment: steroids, IVIG, rituximab, splenectomy for refractory cases
CT scan of the abdomen with contrast • Location of injury and gross hematuria suggest kidney injury • Contrast is really excreted and is used to visualize the collecting system
Intravenous administration of calcium gluconate • Hypocalcemia after parathyroidectomy is transient, but IV calcium should be given to protect the heart
Slipped capital femoral epiphysis • Classically presents in teens/pre-teens that are obese or above 90th percentile in weight

Carotid duplex ultrasonography • Bilateral carotid bruits indicate stenosis in the carotids → compromised blood flow → cerebral ischemia → TIA • Carotid U/S should be performed to determine the level of stenosis and the corresponding treatment
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head • Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease • Common in males between 5-8 years old

Malignant pleural effusion • Past hx of cancer, respiratory distress, cyanotic, cachectic, decreased breath sounds, dullness to percussion • Pleural friction rub could be due to post-radiation fibrosis of the lungs
Cholangitis, ascending • Charcot's triad: jaundice, fever, RUQ pain • Reynolds pentad: Charcot's triad, altered mental status, hypotension • ↑ alkaline phosphatase and ↑ conjugated bilirubin

Determination of ankle brachial indices • ABl is the preferred initial step in diagnosis of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) • Arterial U/S of the lower extremities is less sensitive and specific than ABI for the diagnosis
Melanoma • Subungual hematoma, unlike melanoma, will gradually clear as the nail heals • Subungual hematoma will form a transverse groove across the surface as the nail heals
